cases.expected_boundary: Unresolved owner-required product meaning yields needs_input and at most three questions.
A missing, stale, rejected, or mismatched owner decision cannot close an owner-gated profile.
A changed hash-bound source invalidates the active gate.
A genuinely passive screen is allowed only with an exact source-bound no_actions_reason; a visible control without an outcome is rejected.
Native-image comparison proves image comparison only and never silently upgrades to source fidelity.
Mobile-specific evidence or composition cannot close a Web-only program without exact current authorization.
External, destructive, or paid execution requires mocked_external, network_mock evidence, isolated network, and redaction.
Historical contracts remain readable but cannot close an active G0-G6 profile.
Hash-correct opaque bytes cannot substitute for a native capture, renderable candidate, review board, or inheritance report at G3.
A G4 family aggregate rejects a hashable file that is not a typed rendered family review surface.
A G5 wave aggregate rejects a hashable file that is not a typed rendered wave review surface.
A readiness transition rejects hash-correct opaque bytes in place of a typed check-specific preflight document.
An awaiting_input row resumes only from a typed owner-input response bound to the exact decision packet, not from arbitrary readable text.
Changing the current G3 candidate artifact invalidates every anchor capture until typed render provenance is regenerated against the new candidate hash.
A same-program canonical owner decision for another artifact identity, revision, profile, path, hash, or natural-language input cannot resume the current visual stage.
Typed preflight evidence still fails when a source binding, allowed write scope, or handoff hash is semantically false.
A change record for one accepted artifact cannot be attached to another ledger anchor to under- or over-invalidate dependencies.
An active, awaiting-input, or blocked ledger exposes only the one live state allowed by its current_stage.
A terminal ledger has no pending live authority, explains skipped rows, and retains an accepted successor for every invalidated row.
Every shard-index path, outer hash, entry hash, JSON pointer, and identity is resolved before a bounded context may claim an exact read-set label.
An accepted row revalidates the decision, outgoing transition, preserved typed response, decision packet, reviewed artifact, and natural-language input as one immutable chain.
Current-authority G4 and G5 targets exact-cover every live family and wave, including multi-family and multi-wave programs.

Each G5 directly depends on every current-authority G4 row plus its declared prerequisite waves; a G5 claim or ready transition is blocked until all current G4 rows are accepted; G6 directly depends on every live G5 row.
G3 cannot pass until every geometry receipt binds the exact validated representative shell screen contract and screen revision used by production capture.
G3 render provenance and geometry must use the reference or implementation logical artifact ID declared by the active shell contract comparison claims.
Every preserved G0-G2 product answer is SHA-256-bound by the accepted ledger row, so its natural-language meaning cannot be rewritten after acceptance.
The final G3 validator independently cross-binds geometry render-source, main-response, logical-artifact, screenshot, provenance, and live artifact hashes.
Every G3-G6 owner review HTML surface binds and visibly exact-covers a typed hash-pinned manifest of the artifacts actually being accepted.
The active G3 shell contract must bind the current program revision, visual authority, intake, baseline, responsive anchors, and representative screen coverage.
A raster receipt is recomputed from the live decoded PNG pixels; editing pixel counts or pass status cannot close visual acceptance.
Reference and implementation PNGs, render provenance, geometry, and source artifacts remain readable and hash-bound through final visual acceptance.
Every accepted ledger row pins the exact outgoing transition receipt SHA-256, while visual gates also revalidate their complete nested artifact closure.
Accepted G3-G6 rows revalidate the nested review manifest and its live artifact hashes, so changing a sidecar without changing the outer program cannot preserve acceptance.
A free two-field journey_id/result claim cannot replace a computed, program-bound critical-journey proof with exact accepted screen/state, transition, and wave coverage.
A G6 implementation handoff cannot omit any declared intake, baseline, artifact index, accepted wave, typed journey proof, or canonical reproduction command.
A one-token-per-category baseline with one component cannot close baseline_ready when the accepted pilot inventory contains undispositioned reusable observations.
A genuinely small pilot passes when every observed reusable primitive has exactly one source-backed standard disposition.
Omitting any observed typography clause, including line height, breaks source exact-cover.
A newly observed reusable primitive must be represented by a fixed clause and cannot disappear silently.
A target applicability manifest must exact-cover every baseline clause derived for the independently bound screen identities.
An executor cannot replace a deterministically applicable clause with an invented source-backed-not-applicable disposition.
Duplicate clause IDs and stale clause-inventory hashes fail baseline_ready.
Candidate typography and control metrics are compared with independent pilot clauses even if a screen contract repeats the candidate choices.
Different target content and screen-specific composition may pass while every applicable reusable clause remains exact.
A typed exception applies only to its exact clause IDs and cannot excuse unrelated mismatches.
A visual-authority reference remains provenance-only while the target implementation alone receives screen and standard conformance gates.
Target actions, regions, fixtures, accessibility, keyboard, and overflow obligations cannot be reintroduced on a novel-screen visual reference.
Stage and adjacent-stage readiness reject a G3 result without the standard board and exact standard lineage.
Historical contracts remain readable, but an older sparse baseline cannot authorize a current active proof chain.
G3-G6 review manifests exact-cover the standard-conformance evidence nested in the artifact being accepted.
A prepared historical migration cannot apply after the exact source ledger bytes change.
A historical migration candidate is rejected when more than one live row carries an executor claim.
A historical prompt, receipt, decision, or evidence artifact cannot change after the migration receipt binds it.
The successor topology must bind the exact pre-migration ledger and released registry, never its own prospective output.
